meta.title: One System, One Frame
meta.subtitle: Two switches ANDed in a single if, and a one-bit latch that turns the result into edges

views.label: What happens exactly once
views.note: Creation and destruction are not part of the frame. They bracket every frame the system will ever see.

views.label: The gate is one if statement
views.note: A bit you own, ANDed with a query emptiness test. Either being false skips your update and nothing else.

views.label: The latch that makes edges
views.note: A single stored bit remembers last frame's answer, so the stop callback fires on the falling edge only.

states.label: OnDestroy
states.tag: always, even if it never ran

cards.title: The gate, literally
items: One condition decides everything: the enabled bit AND the requirement test · SystemBase.cs:187
An unmanaged system uses the identical condition · WorldUnmanaged.cs:892
Enabled is a single bit in the system's flag word · SystemState.cs:179
The requirement test returns true immediately when nothing was required · SystemState.cs:698

cards.title: What the gate does not do
items: It does not remove the system from its group; the group still walks it every frame
It does not undo the sort, so turning it back on costs nothing
It does not skip OnCreate, which already ran at world construction
A disabled system is a branch not taken, not a system that is gone

cards.title: The latch is an edge detector
items: One stored bit remembers whether the system ran last frame
Rising edge: the bit is set and the start callback fires once · SystemBase.cs:202
Falling edge: pending jobs are completed and the stop callback fires once · SystemBase.cs:227, :233
So the two running callbacks are edges, and OnUpdate is the level

cards.title: The requirement test ignores filters
items: Every required query is checked with an ignore-filter emptiness test · SystemState.cs:673
So enableable components and shared component filters cannot close the gate
A system can pass the gate and then process zero entities, correctly and every frame
Requiring a component that exists but is disabled everywhere still lets the system run
